The legal issues presented in the paragraph involve a challenge to the local government's regulatory authority and the substantive rights of the fishing companies. Specifically, the companies are raising two primary legal questions: first, whether the government possesses the statutory or constitutional authority to impose catch quotas for the purpose of preserving marine life; and second, whether such regulations constitute an infringement upon their vested rights to conduct business, potentially raising issues related to due process, takings clauses, or freedom of commerce depending on the jurisdiction.

Regarding your priority question, a typical year has 365 days.
